timing: Written before this profile/fit. All source outcomes, including the two latest confirmations, were already seen. This entire analysis is posthoc.
question: Can the fixed cooling rate and common load response explain the remaining error, separately from idle background/preparation history?
family: Reuse preparation-memory-v1: T'=beta*(E-T)+k*u+H; H'=-H/30. Same original relative state slopes u. gamma fixed zero; no new heat circuit or delay family.

fit.beta_multipliers: 61 log-spaced values from 0.2 to 5 times original beta, including 1 exactly
fit.gain: one nonnegative analytic least-squares k per beta; no cap
fit.objective: development post-load AP MSE; ties lower beta
fit.boundary: report boundary optimum; do not expand grid after seeing results
fit.interpretation: finite diagnostic range, not physiological bounds

identification.profile: all beta/k values and preload conditions; best RMSE+0.05C range is a descriptive sensitivity set, NOT CI or PASS
identification.local: normalized numerical Jacobian of log(beta),log(k), rank and correlation; not global physical identifiability
identification.state_basis: per-state unit-response SVD at original beta; no per-state refit
identification.control: archived no-work resident C: observed baseline to +35s initializes E/H, later samples are targets. No workload start is invented. A zero load basis returns gain=null.
identification.limits: Single development session, effective reference not ambient, AP alone cannot label both idle exponential rates as physical components

control_pair: Existing C/L retained as descriptive observations. L lacks required 55s pre-load history and is excluded from candidate scores, not from the evidence inventory.
alignment: Common-origin fixed windows plus time since last lane release. No causal subtraction between unmatched sessions/APKs; no alignment by observed peak.
candidate_policy: At most one development-selected diagnostic candidate. Preserve the old candidate and frozen model; no outcome-driven family search or re-fit on confirmation. No automatic adoption.
